note: An intermediate guitar plus theory and ear week at 30 minutes a day: 7th chords and the ii-V-I are heard, named, played as shapes, arpeggios and guide tones, moved to a new key and improvised over, with an ear or theory exercise every day between the guitar work. Each step says what to press and where to look.

plan.title: Week 1: 7th chords and the ii-V-I
plan.summary: Hear and name 7th chords, then play the ii-V-I as shapes, arpeggios, guide tones and solos in C and G, with the relative minor and a blues for contrast.

exercises.title: Dm7, G7, Cmaj7 shapes
exercises.focus: Open ii-V-I shapes in C · slow changes
exercises.why: These three shapes are the ii-V-I in C, the most common chord move in jazz and many ballads.

sections.text: Press a chord box to hear it. Fret each shape, then pick the strings one at a time to check they ring. Change from Dm7 to G7 to Cmaj7 slowly, four strums each.

exercises.title: Name the chord
exercises.focus: Major, minor, 7, maj7, m7 by ear
exercises.why: Naming a chord's quality by ear is the skill behind working out songs.

sections.text: Press Start. The game plays a chord. Pick its name. Listen to the top note: a half step under the octave means maj7, a whole step means 7 or m7. The tally under the answers keeps your score.

exercises.title: Arpeggios of the ii-V-I
exercises.focus: Dm7, G7 and Cmaj7 arpeggios, one position each
exercises.why: An arpeggio is the chord one note at a time, so a solo built from it outlines the changes.

sections.text: Dm7
Press Play on the click above. Play the Dm7 arpeggio up and down, one note per click: {{1}} {{b3}} {{5}} {{b7}}.
G7
G7: {{1}} {{3}} {{5}} {{b7}}. Lean on its {{3}} (B) and {{b7}} (F): these two notes pull toward Cmaj7.
Cmaj7
Cmaj7: {{1}} {{3}} {{5}} {{7}}. Then play all three arpeggios in a row, one bar each, without stopping.

exercises.title: Comp the ii-V-I
exercises.focus: Dm7-G7-Cmaj7-Cmaj7 with the band at 80
exercises.why: Comping means playing the chords in rhythm under a melody, and short, light strums leave room for it.

sections.text: Two strums a bar
Press Play. The lit block shows the chord. Strum short chords on beats 2 and 4, one bar each.
Bass and chord
Press Play. Now pick each chord's root on beats 1 and 3. Strum the top strings on beats 2 and 4.

exercises.title: Alternate picking
exercises.focus: Down-up, three notes per string, 90 bpm
exercises.why: Three notes per string puts the pick on alternating strokes at each string crossing.

sections.text: Press Play on the click. Pick three notes per string, down-up, across all six strings and back.

exercises.title: ii, V and I in the scale
exercises.focus: C major · chords on 2, 5 and 1
exercises.why: Stack 3rds on the 2nd, 5th and 1st notes of C major and you get Dm7, G7 and Cmaj7.

sections.text: Build them
Tap a note on the staff to hear it. Tap {{2}} {{4}} {{6}} {{1}}: Dm7, every other note from D. Then {{5}} {{7}} {{2}} {{4}}: G7. Then {{1}} {{3}} {{5}} {{7}}: Cmaj7.
Hear the pull
Press Play and listen. The ii moves away, the V leans hard, the I lands. Say each numeral as it arrives.

exercises.title: Guide tones on the guitar
exercises.focus: 3rds and 7ths through Dm7-G7-Cmaj7
exercises.why: The 3rd and 7th of each chord move by a half step or not at all, so two notes are enough to make the changes heard.

sections.text: The 3rd-7th line
Press Play. Play along from the tab, one note per beat: F over Dm7 (its 3rd), F over G7 (its 7th), E over Cmaj7 (its 3rd).
The 7th-3rd line
Now the other line: C over Dm7 (its 7th), B over G7 (its 3rd), B over Cmaj7 (its 7th). Then switch between the two lines.

exercises.title: Improvise on the guide tones
exercises.focus: Dm7-G7-Cmaj7 · land on 3rds and 7ths
exercises.why: Starting each chord on a guide tone is the quickest way to make a solo follow the changes.

sections.text: Land on the targets
Press Play. Improvise in C major. Land on a lit target when each chord comes round.
Fewer notes
Same backing. Now use only three or four notes per chord. Include its guide tone each time.

exercises.title: Legato warm-up
exercises.focus: Legato trill · fingers 1-3 · G string, 5th fret
exercises.why: Hammer-ons and pull-offs build left-hand strength without the pick.

sections.text: Press Play on the click. Pick once, then hammer finger 3 and pull off to finger 1, one note per click. Rest when the hand gets tired, then go again.

exercises.title: C major and A minor, same notes
exercises.focus: C major → A natural minor over one click
exercises.why: A minor uses exactly the notes of C major; only the home note changes, and with it the mood.

sections.text: Hear the home move
Press Play. Only the click sounds. Play C major from C for four bars. Then play the same notes from A for four bars: A minor. Where does each one come to rest?
La is home
Tap {{1}} (A) on the staff to hear it. Walk up to the C above it. In C major that C is Do; here it is the {{b3}}. A minor is C major starting from La.

exercises.title: One shape, two keys
exercises.focus: A minor pentatonic position 1 = C major pentatonic
exercises.why: The relative minor works on the neck too: one pentatonic position serves both keys, with a different root.

sections.text: As A minor
Press Play on the click above. Play position 1 at the 5th fret up and down. Start and end on {{1}} (A).
As C major
The same frets, but now home is {{1}} (C). Start and end there. Hear how bright it sounds.

exercises.title: Major or minor song?
exercises.focus: C-G-Am-F vs Am-F-C-G by ear and by hand
exercises.why: The same four chords can sound major or minor depending on which one feels like home.

sections.text: Start on C
Press Play. The lit block shows the chord: C, G, Am, F, one bar each. Strum along. Notice that C feels like home.
Start on Am
Now Am, F, C, G: the same chords, but Am is home and it sounds minor. Strum along. Then stop: which chord feels finished?

exercises.title: Am7, D7, Gmaj7 shapes
exercises.focus: Open ii-V-I shapes in G
exercises.why: The same move in a new key: Am7 is ii, D7 is V, Gmaj7 is I in G.

sections.text: Press a chord box to hear it. Fret each shape and pick the strings to check they ring. Then change from Am7 to D7 to Gmaj7, four strums each.

exercises.title: b7 or 7?
exercises.focus: Minor 7th vs major 7th by ear
exercises.why: The 7th is what separates D7 from Gmaj7, and hearing it alone makes the chords easy to name.

sections.text: Press Start. The game plays an interval. Pick its name: a minor 7th (as in D7) or a major 7th (as in Gmaj7).

exercises.title: Arpeggios in G
exercises.focus: Am7, D7 and Gmaj7 arpeggios
exercises.why: Moving the arpeggios to G shows they are shapes of degrees, not lists of frets.

sections.text: Am7 and D7
Press Play on the click above. Play the Am7 arpeggio up and down, one note per click: {{1}} {{b3}} {{5}} {{b7}}.
Gmaj7, then all three
Gmaj7: {{1}} {{3}} {{5}} {{7}}. Then play all three arpeggios in a row, one bar each.

exercises.title: Solo over ii-V-I in G
exercises.focus: Am7-D7-Gmaj7 · guide tones as targets
exercises.why: Guide tones work the same in a new key: C to C to B, or G to F♯ to F♯.

sections.text: Guide tones only
Press Play. Play only the targets, one long note per chord. Pick either line.
Fill in around them
Same backing. Now improvise in G major. Still land on a target at each change. Record the last two minutes.

exercises.title: Picking, skip a string
exercises.focus: Down-up string skipping at 80 bpm
exercises.why: Arpeggios jump strings, so the pick hand needs to jump accurately.

sections.text: Press Play on the click. Pick two notes per string, down-up, skipping a string each time.

exercises.title: Chord qualities, faster
exercises.focus: Name 7th chords, 30 seconds a round
exercises.why: Answering quickly makes chord hearing work at song speed.

sections.text: Press Start. The game plays a chord. Pick its name as fast as you can for 30 seconds, then rest. Can you beat your tally from day 1?

exercises.title: Which numeral?
exercises.focus: I-vi-ii-V in C by ear
exercises.why: I-vi-ii-V adds the vi to the ii-V-I, and it is the loop under countless songs.

sections.text: With the chart
Press Play and listen. Say each numeral as it arrives: I (Cmaj7), vi (Am7), ii (Dm7), V (G7).
In a new order
Now the same four chords in a new order. Look away and press Play. Write down the numerals you hear, then check.

exercises.title: Comp I-vi-ii-V
exercises.focus: Cmaj7-Am7-Dm7-G7 · three comping feels
exercises.why: Playing one loop with different comping feels is how a rhythm part stays interesting.

sections.text: Block chords on 2 and 4
Press Play. The lit block shows the chord. Strum short chords on beats 2 and 4.
Bass and chord
Press Play. Pick the root on beats 1 and 3. Strum the chord on beats 2 and 4.
Arpeggiated
Press Play. Pick each chord low to high in eighth notes. Let the notes ring.

exercises.title: Legato, fingers 2-4
exercises.focus: Legato trill · fingers 2-4 · B string, 7th fret
exercises.why: The weaker finger pair needs the most work.

sections.text: Press Play on the click. Pick once, then hammer finger 4 and pull off to finger 2, one note per click. Rest when the hand gets tired, then go again.

exercises.title: Why blues uses three 7ths
exercises.focus: A7, D7, E7 as I7, IV7, V7
exercises.why: Blues breaks the rule of one dominant per key: every chord is a 7th, which gives the style its restless sound.

sections.text: The three chords
A7, D7 and E7 are built on {{1}}, {{4}} and {{5}} of A. Tap those notes on the staff to hear them. Then press each chord box: the same dominant colour three times.
A7's own notes
Tap the A7 arpeggio: {{1}} {{3}} {{5}} {{b7}}. Its {{3}} is C♯, which is not in A minor pentatonic. That clash is the sound of the blues.

exercises.title: Twelve-bar in A
exercises.focus: 12-bar blues with A7, D7, E7 at 90 bpm
exercises.why: The twelve-bar form is a fixed road map: learn it once and you can join any blues jam.

sections.text: Follow the form
Press Play. The lit block shows the chord: four bars of A7, two of D7, two of A7, then E7, D7, A7, E7. Strum along. Count the bars out loud.
Without counting
Same form. Pick the bass note on beats 1 and 3. Strum on beats 2 and 4. Keep going without counting out loud.

exercises.title: Solo with the 3rd
exercises.focus: A minor pentatonic + C♯ over A7-D7
exercises.why: Adding the chord's 3rd to the pentatonic position makes a blues solo follow the changes.

sections.text: Slide into C♯
Press Play on the backing below. Improvise in position 1. When A7 comes round, slide from {{b3}} (C) up to {{c-sharp}}: the 3rd of A7, not in A minor pentatonic. End your phrases on {{1}}.
Over D7
Same backing. When D7 comes round, aim for {{d}}. When A7 comes round, keep sliding into {{c-sharp}}.

days.theme: Review: the week in one jam

exercises.title: ii-V-I shapes in C and G
exercises.focus: Dm7-G7-Cmaj7 then Am7-D7-Gmaj7
exercises.why: Both keys back to back shows the shapes are under your fingers.

sections.text: Press a chord box to hear it. Play four strums per chord: the ii-V-I in C, then in G. Change keys without stopping.

exercises.title: Ear check
exercises.focus: Chord qualities, scored by the tally
exercises.why: The week's ear work as a score to beat next week.

sections.text: Press Start. The game plays a chord. Pick its name. Play a few rounds, then compare the tally with days 1 and 5.

exercises.title: Arpeggios from memory
exercises.focus: Dm7-G7-Cmaj7 arpeggios without the chart
exercises.why: Playing them without help is the test that the shapes are yours.

sections.text: Without looking
Press Play. Play each arpeggio from memory as its chord comes round: root, 3rd, 5th, 7th, one note per beat. Look away from the tab.
Check and fix
Switch to the neck view and check every note. Replay any chord you missed.

exercises.title: ii-V-I jam
exercises.focus: Guide tones, then free soloing over Dm7-G7-Cmaj7
exercises.why: Guide tones, arpeggios and the scale together are what make a solo over changes sound sure.

sections.text: Guide tones
Press Play. Play one guide tone per chord, either line from day 2.
Arpeggio phrases
Same backing. Start each chord with a run up its arpeggio. Then leave space.
Free, and record
Improvise freely. Still land on a target at each change. Record it and keep it for next week.
